name: Panasonic Holdings Corporation (パナソニックホールディングス) — focus: Panasonic Energy Co., Ltd.
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Panasonic is pivoting Tesla-built EV-cell capacity into the AI boom — data-center energy storage (rack-mounted BBUs) is now the group's flagship growth story, with a claimed ~80% share of data-center distributed power systems, a ¥800B FY2029 sales target the CEO calls 'a minimum commitment,' and Kansas EV lines being repurposed to data-center cells. BACKGROUND: Founded 1918; holding-company structure since 2022 with Panasonic Energy (est. April 2022, battery roots to 1931) as the battery arm. EV cylindrical cells (2170 at Nevada ~41 GWh/yr and Kansas, 4680 readiness at Wakayama), consumer/industrial batteries, and six group segments. Fiscal years end March 31. Fiscal 2026 group net sales ¥8,048.7B (−4.8%) with operating profit down 44.6% on Group Management Reform restructuring (~12,000 job cuts); Q1 fiscal 2027 (Apr–Jun 2026) was the best Q1 operating profit in 41 years on AI-infrastructure demand.
ecosystemRole: We assess Panasonic's ecosystem position as the incumbent of data-center backup power rather than grid-scale BESS: it does not appear in grid-storage integrator rankings, but claims ~80% of the data-center distributed-power (BBU) market, with orders covering >80% of its FY2029 ¥800B data-center storage target. Next-generation Capacitor Backup Units (supercapacitors, with Panasonic Industry) map directly onto NVIDIA's rack-side storage tier. Q1 fiscal 2027 data-center storage sales were ¥113B (1.9× YoY); the FY2027 forecast is ¥550B.

productsAndServices.name: Data-Center Energy Storage (BBU / CBU)
productsAndServices.description: Rack-mounted Battery Backup Units — Li-ion cells and storage modules providing blackout backup and peak shaving against AI-server load spikes — plus next-generation Capacitor Backup Units (supercapacitors) co-developed with Panasonic Industry. Investment program: ¥350B (~$2.2B) FY2026–FY2028 within a ¥500B AI-infrastructure envelope; Kansas De Soto lines repurposed from EV to data-center cells; module capacity expanding in Mexico (existing lines + new nearby plant) and Japan (cell capacity ×3 by FY2029 vs FY2026).
highlights: Company claims ~80% market share in data-center distributed power supply systems, with orders covering >80% of planned FY2029 sales
FY2029 target: ¥800B of data-center storage revenue — CEO Kazuo Tadanobu: 'a minimum commitment,' expecting >¥1T
Q1 fiscal 2027 data-center storage sales ¥113B (1.9× YoY); FY2027 forecast ¥550B (1.7× FY2026)
Customers described only as unnamed hyperscalers; trade press reports both Panasonic and Samsung SDI supply-short in BBU cells
productsAndServices.positioning: The BBU incumbent vs Samsung SDI's challenger position; the CBU supercapacitor roadmap targets the rack-side transient tier NVIDIA's GB300 architecture created. Not a grid-scale BESS player — no presence in integrator rankings.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct B2B supply to hyperscalers and server OEMs
productsAndServices.roadmap: US data-center battery production from fiscal 2028 (Kansas); 2nd Mexico module site mass-producing FY2027, 3rd FY2028

productsAndServices.name: EV Cylindrical Cells (2170 / 4680)
productsAndServices.description: 2170 cells from Nevada (~41 GWh/yr, >11B cells to date) and Kansas De Soto (opened July 2025, ~32 GWh target, ~20% higher productivity — full-capacity date abandoned amid the Tesla slump); ~800 Wh/L claimed density, ~19B cells cumulative, zero vehicle recalls claimed. 4680: 'mass-production readiness' declared September 2024 at the Wakayama mother factory; no first-party full-ramp confirmation since. Publicized customers: Lucid, Subaru, Mazda, Harbinger, Zoox (robotaxis); Tesla is the widely understood but first-party-unnamed anchor.
highlights: North American auto-battery sales plan cut 13% to 40 GWh (October 2025) as US EV credits ended
¥40B one-time charge for 2170 manufacturing defects for an unnamed customer (charging failures, not fire risk — widely inferred to be Tesla, not company-confirmed)
Sila US silicon-anode supply agreement for ~5% capacity-boosted cells at Kansas
productsAndServices.positioning: #7 global EV battery share (3.7% in 2025, SNE) — slipped below SK On; the only top player that shrank in 2024. Tesla concentration is the structural risk trade press consistently flags.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct OEM supply from Japan and US plants
productsAndServices.targetSegments: US/Japan EV OEMs, robotaxis (Zoox), medium-duty EVs (Harbinger)
productsAndServices.roadmap: 4680 ramp unconfirmed; Oklahoma third-plant plan dropped (2023); Kansas partial conversion to data-center cells

productsAndServices.name: Group Segments (Connect, Electric Works, HVAC, Industry, Smart Life)
productsAndServices.description: Beyond Energy: Connect (supply-chain software/avionics), Electric Works, HVAC & Cooling (¥1,312B fiscal 2026 sales), Industry (capacitors and MEGTRON multilayer PCB materials for AI servers — Thailand capacity doubling), and Smart Life. Automotive was deconsolidated in fiscal 2025; Housing sold to YKK in March 2026; the TV business partnered with Skyworth for Europe.
highlights: Panasonic Industry's MEGTRON PCB materials are a second AI-infrastructure exposure line
Group Management Reform: ~12,000 job cuts, ¥174.5B fiscal 2026 restructuring cost, ROE 10% target by FY2029

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess the data-center storage pivot is Panasonic's core strategy, not a hedge: ¥350B of dedicated capex, EV lines physically repurposed, Japan cell capacity tripling by FY2029, and a CEO calling ¥800B of FY2029 revenue 'a minimum commitment.' Basis: company filings, strategy publication, and investor briefing.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the ~80% distributed-power share claim is plausible but self-reported — no third-party verification exists, and Samsung SDI's UPS/BBU push plus reported industry-wide BBU cell shortages suggest the moat will be contested as the market grows toward ~$7B by 2033 (analyst estimates).

(High confidence) We assess Tesla concentration remains the EV business's defining risk: Kansas ramp decisions tracked Tesla's sales slump, the ¥40B defect charge is widely inferred to involve the 2170 anchor customer, and first-party channels conspicuously avoid naming Tesla while publicizing Lucid/Subaru/Mazda/Zoox diversification.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the group restructuring (12,000 cuts, segment dissolutions, Housing sale) is the financing mechanism for the AI pivot — fiscal 2026's −44.6% OP was deliberately absorbed to reset the cost base before the FY2027 rebound guidance (adj. OP ¥650B), which the record Q1 supports.

(Low confidence) The 4680 program's status is a genuine unknown: mass-production readiness was declared September 2024 with no first-party ramp confirmation since — treat any 4680 volume claims as unverified.
